memories.author: D03
memories.text:
Initial assessment for vitamin D deficiency.
PRESENTING COMPLAINT: The patient reports fatigue and occasional bone aches over the past 2 months.
EXAMINATION: BP 138/84 mmHg, weight 68 kg, height 1.55 m, BMI 28.3 (obese). General appearance well, no pallor.
IMPRESSION: Vitamin D deficiency likely contributing to fatigue. No other acute issues.
ARRANGEMENTS: Start cholecalciferol 60000 IU once weekly for 8 weeks, then 1000 IU daily. Advise weight-bearing exercise and calcium-rich diet. Return if new bone pain, worsening fatigue, or fever >39°C.

memories.author: D03
memories.text: Cholecalciferol 60000 IU oral once weekly for 8 weeks, then cholecalciferol 1000 IU oral daily.

memories.author: lab
memories.text: Serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D: 14 ng/mL (ref 30-100). Serum calcium: 9.2 mg/dL (ref 8.6-10.3). Serum phosphate: 2.8 mg/dL (ref 2.5-4.5).

memories.author: patient
memories.text: Started the weekly high-dose vitamin D. Feel a bit less tired after two weeks, but still get mild back ache after long shifts at the hotel.

memories.author: lab
memories.text: Serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D: 28 ng/mL (ref 30-100). Serum calcium: 9.4 mg/dL. Serum phosphate: 3.0 mg/dL.

memories.author: D03
memories.text:
Follow-up on vitamin D repletion.
PRESENTING COMPLAINT: Persistent mild fatigue and occasional back discomfort.
EXAMINATION: BP 136/82 mmHg, weight 67 kg, BMI 27.9 (overweight). No tenderness.
IMPRESSION: Vitamin D level still suboptimal; continue supplementation.
ARRANGEMENTS: Switch to cholecalciferol 1000 IU daily indefinitely. Advise daily walk and fortified milk. Return if fatigue worsens, new pain, or fever >39°C.

memories.author: front_desk
memories.text: Booked follow-up visit for 2025-12-10 at 10:00 AM with Dr Priya Natarajan.

memories.author: D03
memories.text:
Routine check.
PRESENTING COMPLAINT: Patient feels better, less fatigue.
EXAMINATION: BP 134/80 mmHg, weight 66 kg, BMI 27.5 (overweight).
IMPRESSION: Vitamin D likely adequate now; monitor.
ARRANGEMENTS: Continue cholecalciferol 1000 IU daily. Encourage sunlight exposure 15 mins daily. Return if bone pain, fatigue, or fever >39°C.

memories.author: lab
memories.text: Serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D: 34 ng/mL (ref 30-100). Serum calcium: 9.5 mg/dL. Serum phosphate: 3.1 mg/dL.

memories.author: D03
memories.text:
Annual review.
PRESENTING COMPLAINT: No specific complaints.
EXAMINATION: BP 132/78 mmHg, weight 65 kg, BMI 27.0 (overweight).
IMPRESSION: Vitamin D sufficient. Annual fasting lipid profile and glucose ordered per protocol.
ARRANGEMENTS: Continue cholecalciferol 1000 IU daily. Lipid and glucose labs today. Return if chest pain, breathlessness, fever >39°C.

memories.author: D03
memories.text: ECG: Normal sinus rhythm, rate 78 bpm. No ST-T changes. No evidence of ischemia.

memories.author: D03
memories.text:
Mid-year follow-up.
PRESENTING COMPLAINT: Patient reports occasional knee pain after standing long hours.
EXAMINATION: BP 130/76 mmHg, weight 64 kg, BMI 26.6 (overweight). Knee exam mild tenderness, no effusion.
IMPRESSION: Vitamin D adequate; knee pain likely mechanical.
ARRANGEMENTS: Continue cholecalciferol 1000 IU daily. Advise quadriceps strengthening, weight control. Return if swelling, redness, fever >39°C.

memories.author: lab
memories.text: Serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D: 36 ng/mL (ref 30-100). Serum calcium: 9.5 mg/dL. Serum phosphate: 3.2 mg/dL.
